steps.label: Document All Violations
steps.details: Photograph all violations with timestamps. Save all landlord communications. Note dates and health impacts. Ohio does not require written leases — month-to-month oral leases are valid.
steps.deadline: Document immediately — Ohio eviction timeline is extremely fast

steps.label: Send Written Repair Notice
steps.details: Ohio Landlord-Tenant Act (ORC §5321.07): send written notice to landlord. Landlord has reasonable time — 30 days standard, less for emergency. After notice expires: tenant may terminate lease, make repairs and deduct up to one month's rent, or sue for damages. Send certified mail.
steps.deadline: PREREQUISITE before withholding rent or repair-and-deduct

steps.label: File Code Enforcement Complaint
steps.details: Contact local code enforcement: Columbus 311 (614-645-3111), Cleveland Housing Court/Building Dept (216-664-2493), Cincinnati Neighborhood Services (513-591-6000). Request written inspection report — critical evidence.

steps.label: Contact Legal Aid Immediately — Same Day for Eviction
steps.details: Ohio's eviction timeline is too fast to wait. Contact legal aid the day you receive any notice.
steps.deadline: Contact same day as any eviction notice — do not wait for hearing

steps.label: Assert Retaliation Protection
steps.details: ORC §5321.02: landlord cannot increase rent, decrease services, or file eviction in retaliation for good-faith habitability complaint or code enforcement contact. 90-day presumption period.

steps.label: Document Wages Owed
steps.details: Gather pay stubs, time records, offer letter. Ohio minimum wage: $10.45/hr (2025). Overtime: 1.5x after 40 hrs (FLSA). Final paycheck: Ohio Prompt Pay Act (ORC §4113.15) — due by next regularly scheduled payday after separation. Employer owes 6% penalty per month on late final pay.
steps.deadline: Ohio SOL: 2 years from date wages were due

steps.label: Send Written Wage Demand
steps.details: Formal written demand specifying hours, rate, total owed. Final paycheck demand triggers 6% monthly penalty under Ohio Prompt Pay Act.
steps.deadline: Final pay due by next scheduled payday after separation

steps.label: File Ohio DOL Complaint
steps.details: Ohio Department of Commerce, Division of Labor and Worker Safety: 614-644-2239. Handles minimum wage and Prompt Pay Act violations. 2-year SOL.

steps.label: File Federal WHD Simultaneously
steps.details: Federal WHD Columbus: 614-224-6670. FLSA allows liquidated (double) damages. File same day as Ohio DOL.

steps.label: Review Notice of Action
steps.details: Read the Agency Action Notice carefully. Note: reason, effective date, appeal deadline (usually 30 days for Ohio state benefits). For UI: 21-day deadline from mailing date.
steps.deadline: Appeal deadline on notice — typically 30 days for benefits, 21 days for UI

steps.label: Request State Hearing + Aid-Continuing
steps.details: File written hearing request within 30 days of notice. CRITICAL: simultaneously request continuation of benefits during appeal. Ohio: benefits continue during appeal if timely requested.
steps.deadline: 30 days from notice — FATAL for most programs

steps.label: Prepare and Attend Hearing
steps.details: Contact legal aid for representation before hearing. Request case record 2 weeks before hearing date. Gather all supporting documents, medical records, employment records.
steps.deadline: Request case file 2 weeks before hearing

steps.label: Ohio UI Appeals (ODJFS)
steps.details: 21-day appeal deadline — shorter than neighboring states. ODJFS unemployment appeal: 877-644-6562. Review Commission for further appeal. Circuit Court appeal within 30 days of Review Commission decision.

steps.label: Document Denial
steps.details: Gather denial letter/EOB, policy, medical records, physician letter of medical necessity.

steps.label: File Internal Appeal
steps.details: File with insurer within 180 days of denial. For Ohio Medicaid managed care: file grievance within 90 days. Request all documentation insurer relied upon.
steps.deadline: 180 days from denial (private) · 90 days (Medicaid managed care)

steps.label: Ohio Department of Insurance (ODI) Complaint / External Review
steps.details: If internal appeal denied: file ODI complaint and request external review. Ohio has independent external review — 30 business days for non-urgent, 72 hours for urgent. ODI Consumer Hotline: 800-686-1526.

steps.label: Ohio Medicaid Managed Care — State Fair Hearing
steps.details: Medicaid managed care denial: file state fair hearing request through Ohio JFS within 120 days. Benefits continue during appeal.
steps.deadline: 120 days from managed care denial for state hearing
